articles.title: AUTO-RESEARCH WITH CODEX: HOW I ACHIEVED A 232X FASTER KERNEL OVER BASELINE WITH CODEX IN GPU MODE'S QR_V2 PROBLEM
articles.summary: In a recent auto-research contest focusing on GPU optimizations, an impressive 232x speedup over the baseline was achieved in implementing the batched square compact-Householder QR factorization problem, with the author finishing 12th out of 183 participants. The project involved using techniques like the blocked Householder algorithm, continual kernel profiling, and iteration on ideas presented through advanced AI models.

articles.title: MAXIMIZING THE VALUE OF YOUR CLAUDE CODE SESSIONS
articles.summary: To maximize the efficiency of Claude Code sessions, users should clear prior context when starting new tasks, set the model and effort level early, and use @-mentions for files to reduce unnecessary token usage. Reducing tokens isn't about using fewer overall but making sure the tokens spent directly contribute to the task at hand, as more tokens can accumulate when irrelevant context is included.

articles.title: MODELS ARE GETTING DUMBER ON PURPOSE
articles.summary: Recent advancements in AI models show that while their reasoning capabilities continue to improve per parameter, their factual recall has notably declined, suggesting a deliberate trade-off where knowledge is sacrificed for reasoning skills. This shift allows models to operate effectively by relying on external information sources to provide up-to-date facts, reducing issues like hallucination by enabling the model to reference and verify information against live data rather than fixed weights.

articles.title: SOFTWARE ENGINEERING FUNDAMENTALS MATTER MORE THAN EVER
articles.summary: Software engineering involves carefully navigating choices and problem-solving, especially in the context of AI tools and agentic engineering. While large models show potential in software development, effective coding still relies heavily on human reasoning and thoughtful design for maintainable and debuggable systems.

articles.title: DON'T BE A MEAT PROXY
articles.summary: Using AI-generated responses as a middleman in communication can detract from the value of conversations, as it leads to misunderstanding and unnecessary complexity. Instead of only relaying AI output, individuals should engage with the content, understand it, and respond in their own words to add real value to discussions.

articles.title: WHY DOES OPUS 5 FEEL WORSE TO WORK WITH?
articles.summary: Working with Opus 5 feels less effective compared to its predecessors primarily because it requires more oversight and fails to seek clarification in ambiguous situations. This issue comes from a focus on developing self-improving AI systems that excel on benchmarks, which often focus on bold assumptions over the necessary inquiry and flexibility required in real-life tasks.

articles.title: GLM-5.3: FRONTIER CODING WITH EMERGENT CYBER CAPABILITIES
articles.summary: GLM-5.3 has been released, with improvements in coding capabilities and cyber functions, achieving a 50% enhancement over its predecessor in complex coding tasks and dominating various benchmarks involving vulnerability discovery and exploitation. The model is set to be open-sourced in two weeks after completing safety evaluations.

articles.title: WHO ARE THE TOKEN BROKERS?
articles.summary: “Token brokers" are individuals who purchase unused API credits from startups to resell them. They have commercialized the token relay market. This emerging market is characterized by various online platforms offering discounts on credits for major cloud and inference providers.

articles.title: THE TEMU-FICATION OF SOFTWARE, DIGITAL GOODS & SERVICES
articles.summary: The trend towards the "TEMU-fication" of software and digital goods predicts a future where the majority of content will be produced cheaply by AI, resulting in lower quality and a two-tier market, with human-created products becoming a luxury niche. As mass-produced digital content becomes the norm, it will be needed for consumers to consciously choose between generated and authentic works.

articles.title: A FORTUITOUS DECADE AS AN INDIE SOFTWARE DEVELOPER
articles.summary: After quitting his job in 2016, an indie software developer faced struggles for five years, culminating in a turning point with the release of iOS 15, which revitalized his business and allowed him to rebuild his savings. Despite facing ongoing challenges and not replicating his initial success, he embraces a spontaneous approach to his career, continuing to innovate and adapt without long-term plans.

articles.summary: The image element in HTML can overflow due to properties like `object-fit` and `border-radius`, showing its complexity as both a container and content.

articles.title: EVERYTHING IS ABOUT TO “GO DARK”
articles.summary: The rise of AI in software development could lead to security issues, potentially causing US intelligence and law enforcement agencies to lose critical access to communications and intelligence, resulting in a "going dark" scenario.
